questions.q: Define household industry and state two features that distinguish it from a small-scale industry.
questions.a: A household industry is a manufacturing unit run by family members at home using simple tools and local raw materials with little or no hired labour. Two distinguishing features: (1) Household industries use family labour almost exclusively, while small-scale industries employ hired workers; (2) Household industries have negligible fixed capital (often < ₹1 lakh), whereas small-scale industries have investment up to ₹10 crore (as per MSME Act). A wrong answer that says "both use hired labour" or "both require factory premises" reveals confusion between the two categories and inability to apply the capital/labour threshold criteria.

questions.q: Why are household industries predominantly located in rural areas and small towns rather than in large metropolitan cities? Explain using two geographical factors.
questions.a: Household industries concentrate in rural/small-town areas because: (1) Low-cost family labour and traditional skills are readily available in villages where alternative employment is scarce; (2) They rely on locally sourced raw materials (cotton, clay, bamboo, jute) which are bulky/perishable and expensive to transport to cities. A wrong answer citing "government policy" or "better market access in cities" shows misunderstanding of the resource–labour–cost logic that anchors these industries to their raw material and skill base.

questions.q: A village in West Bengal has 120 households. 40 households make jute handicrafts using family labour and hand tools, selling to a local trader. 15 households run a small jute rope unit with 5 hired workers each and electric motors. Classify each group as household industry or small-scale industry and justify with two criteria per group.
questions.a: Group 1 (40 households): Household industry. Criteria: (a) Production by family members only, no hired labour; (b) Simple hand tools, no power-driven machinery. Group 2 (15 households): Small-scale industry. Criteria: (a) Employs hired workers (5 each); (b) Uses electric motors (power-driven machinery). A wrong classification that puts both in the same category ignores the hired-labour and power-use thresholds that legally and functionally separate the two.

questions.q: Compare the spatial distribution of Khadi (hand-spun, hand-woven cloth) production in Gujarat and handloom weaving in Varanasi. What common geographical factors explain their concentration in these specific regions?
questions.a: Both concentrate due to: (1) Availability of raw cotton (Gujarat) and silk/cotton yarn (Varanasi) locally; (2) Traditional skill clusters passed down through generations (caste/community-based); (3) Supportive institutional infrastructure (Khadi Board in Gujarat, Weaver Service Centres in Varanasi); (4) Humid climate (especially Varanasi) which keeps yarn pliable. A wrong answer that only mentions "government support" or "market demand" misses the physical (climate, raw material) and human (skill inheritance) geography that creates enduring clusters.

questions.q: Evaluate the statement: "Household industries are obsolete in the modern economy because they cannot compete with factory-made goods on price and quality." Provide two arguments for and two against, using Indian evidence.
questions.a: For: (1) Factory goods are cheaper due to economies of scale — e.g., mill-made cloth vs. Khadi; (2) Inconsistent quality and lack of standardisation limit access to formal retail chains. Against: (1) They provide employment to 10+ million artisans (2023 MSME data) with near-zero capital cost — vital for rural livelihood security; (2) Niche markets value uniqueness — e.g., Banarasi silk, Pochampally ikat, Madhubani paintings command premium prices globally. A one-sided answer shows inability to weigh structural economic role against market competitiveness.

questions.q: Design a revival plan for a declining household pottery cluster in Khurja (Uttar Pradesh) that addresses raw material, skill, credit, and market access. List four specific interventions with implementing agencies.
questions.a: 1. Raw material: Set up a common clay processing yard (District Industries Centre + Gram Panchayat). 2. Skill: Introduce electric potter’s wheels and glaze training via MSME Technology Centre, Agra. 3. Credit: Link artisans to MUDRA loans and Artisan Credit Cards (Lead Bank + NABARD). 4. Market: Onboard clusters on GeM portal and organize annual Khurja Pottery Festival (District Administration + Ministry of Textiles). A poor plan that only suggests "give money" or "advertise online" ignores the multi-dimensional (material, skill, finance, market) nature of cluster development.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Household industries (cottage industries) are the smallest ______ units where production is carried out primarily by family members using simple tools, locally available raw materials, and indigenous skills, typically within the home or a small adjoining workspace, with minimal or no hired labour and low capital investment.

Fill in the blank: Observe a weaver in ______ working on a handloom at home: the whole family participates, yarn is sourced locally, tools are simple, and the finished saree is sold to a local trader.
What is Household industries (cottage industries)? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Household industries (cottage industries) are the smallest manufacturing units where production is carried out primarily by family members using simple tools, locally available raw materials, and indigenous skills, typically within the home or a small adjoining workspace, with minimal or no hired labour and low capital investment.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Household industries (cottage industries)?
questions.a: Students often equate "household industry" with "any small business run from home" (e.g., a home-based tuition centre or a freelance graphic designer).

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student can list and explain at least five defining characteristics of household industries, distinguish them from small-scale and large-scale industries using a comparison table, and provide three Indian examples with their regional concentration (e.g., Khadi in Gujarat, handloom weaving in Varanasi, pottery in Khurja).
